headline: Can Meta’s Muse or Grok Bot run my life? I tested both
video_title: Muse vs Grok Bot: Five everyday jobs
comment_question: Which job would you hand over?
deck: Five everyday jobs, one scammer with excellent customer service, and a scorecard that includes what other testers found.
endnote: Field tests run on personal accounts on 20 October 2026. Community reports are attributed individually; company examples are claims. Nothing was sent, booked, bought or cancelled.

figures.after: Muse made the wrong job look beautifully finished.
figures.alt: Grok flags a likely scam; Muse drafts a polished reply.
figures.caption: Scam message reconstructed; Muse’s reply is a redacted crop from the actual draft. Nothing sent.

figures.after: That's quite a lot of Portugal for a trip to New York.
figures.alt: A 29-hour stopover in Lisbon precedes three nights in New York.
figures.caption: Historical fare search, 20 October 2026; Muse’s four-night claim is cropped from the actual interaction.

figures.alt: The article was published in April; Grok presented it as October news.
figures.caption: The April source date and Grok Bot’s October claim are from the test; the public user report is a separate first-week account.

figures.after: I can fix a mistake I know about.
figures.alt: Muse recreated its draft; Gmail still showed two drafts.
figures.caption: Anonymised reconstruction of the draft sequence and independent Gmail readback. Nothing sent.

figures.alt: Five job scores from one personal run per job beside separate findings from the supplied research; missing comparisons remain missing.
figures.caption: The personal runs and supplied research are shown separately. No average or success rate is inferred.
